notes: Curated incident record, UTC. This is the single source for the 90-day bars, the uptime percentage, and the Past Incidents section (assets/status-ui/uptime-bars.js). Each entry was reconstructed from the gateway ledger (gateway_requests per 10-minute bucket), production deploy runs, and the incident notes for that day; times are when the effect actually started and stopped, not when a monitoring issue was opened or closed. severity 'down' = requests were not being served (counts against uptime); 'degraded' = serving with elevated errors or latency (shown, not counted against uptime). Checker incidents opened as GitHub issues AFTER liveIssuesSince are merged in automatically; issue numbers in annulledIssues are monitoring artifacts and ignored.

incidents.title: Elevated gateway errors
incidents.description: Two bursts of gateway-owned `unavailable` errors (23:40–23:59 and 00:50–01:09 UTC), peaking at most requests in a 10-minute window; requests outside the bursts completed normally.

incidents.title: Gateway error burst during catalog reload
incidents.description: About 70% of requests in one 10-minute window failed as `unavailable` while gateway workers picked up a new catalog revision; recovered without intervention.

incidents.title: Elevated errors during repeated catalog publishes
incidents.description: Back-to-back catalog publishes forced gateway workers to rebuild routing state on the request path; requests landing on a rebuilding pod failed as `unavailable` (20–35% of requests). Recurred 10:40–12:50 UTC. Root cause fixed the next day (request path no longer rebuilds the catalog).

incidents.title: Elevated errors during repeated catalog publishes (continued)
incidents.description: Second window of the same catalog-rebuild contention; 20–45% of requests failed as `unavailable` on affected pods.

incidents.title: Requests hung during a large catalog publish
incidents.description: A publish repointing 732 model aliases made every gateway pod rebuild its catalog inline on the request path; requests hung with no response for ~10 minutes (zero accepted requests at 08:53). Fix deployed 17:36 UTC: the request path now only hydrates an already-published snapshot.

incidents.title: Slow responses after catalog repoints
incidents.description: Further alias repoints (08:18–10:15 UTC) triggered the same inline rebuild; ~410 requests took 30 s or longer and surfaced as 503/504 before the fix landed.

incidents.title: Database restart
incidents.description: Production Postgres shut down on an administrator command at 03:51 UTC and came back after crash recovery at 03:58:50. Gateway readiness gates on the database, so /v1 returned 503 and requests were not accepted for ~8 minutes.

incidents.title: Database restart
incidents.description: Signed-in dashboard pages could not load while production Postgres restarted (03:51–03:59 UTC).

incidents.title: Dashboard down after a failed release rollback
incidents.description: A production release failed at the gateway-worker step and its automatic rollback re-applied the web app with an empty environment group, so the dashboard returned errors. The environment was restored by hand at 05:30 UTC.

incidents.title: Free-tier limit checks surfaced as internal errors
incidents.description: A schema change landed before the gateway worker that understood it, so free-tier exhaustion rejections raised an unmapped database error code and were reported as `internal` (~170/min, 30–50% of requests). Cleared when the updated worker rolled at 06:31 UTC; paid traffic was unaffected.

incidents.title: Elevated internal errors
incidents.description: Roughly a third of requests failed inside the gateway as `internal` under a traffic peak (7–9k requests per 10 minutes); recovered after the 17:00 UTC release rolled.

incidents.title: Edge briefly unreachable from external monitoring
incidents.description: External checks timed out for ~13 minutes during a failed release roll (18:18–18:40 UTC); in-flight customer traffic in the ledger continued at normal volume.

incidents.title: Gateway workers restarting on memory pressure
incidents.description: A post-rebuild comparison introduced the previous evening ran after every catalog rebuild while connection changes triggered rebuilds about once a minute, so worker memory ratcheted to its 4 GiB limit and pods restarted repeatedly. About 5% of requests ended incomplete. Mitigated at 09:36 UTC by switching to lean catalog variants; restarts stopped by 09:50.

incidents.title: Slow signed-in pages
incidents.description: Under a signup surge (about 3k per hour), signed-in pages took 3–5 s and intermittently timed out: the grants table lacked an organization index (43.7M rows scanned per read) and the model list made five sequential reads per page. Index built at 10:02 UTC; the list was folded into one read in the same fix.

incidents.title: Edge returned 502 during a failed release
incidents.description: A production release (18:04–18:26 UTC) failed and its rollback left the public edge returning 502; requests were not accepted for ~15 minutes until the previous revision was restored at 18:35.
